items.title: ‘Huge Breakthrough’ in the Math of Imbalance
items.author: Max G. Levy
items.description: For the first time in 30 years, computer scientists have found a better way to allocate objects evenly between two groups. The post ‘Huge Breakthrough’ in the Math of Imbalance first appeared on Quanta Magazine

items.title: Are We Thinking Correctly About AI Intelligence?
items.author: Steven Strogatz and Janna Levin
items.description: Computer scientist Melanie Mitchell discusses why artificial intelligence doesn’t “think” or “reason” like humans, and how we can create better methods for measuring machine cognition. The post Are We Thinking Correctly About AI Intelligence? first appeared on Quanta Magazine

items.title: Building a Quantum Computer, One Fragile Qubit at a Time
items.author: Ben Brubaker
items.description: No one yet knows which technology will power the quantum computers of the future, but the race to create them has already produced some of science’s most intricate machinery. The post Building a Quantum Computer, One Fragile Qubit at a Time first appeared on Quanta Magazine

items.title: Theory of Fluids Enters the 21st Century
items.author: Charlie Wood
items.description: From the 1800s to the early 2000s, physicists used the same theory to understand the behavior of fluids. Now, using a modern insight, they have redefined fluids from the bottom up. The post Theory of Fluids Enters the 21st Century first appeared on Quanta Magazine

items.title: Why Aging May Be a Program, Not a Breakdown
items.author: Ingrid Wickelgren
items.description: By deciphering the molecular signatures of millions of mouse cells, Junyue Cao has found that aging is not haphazard wear and tear but rather a “remodeling of the cell society.” The post Why Aging May Be a Program, Not a Breakdown first appeared on Quanta Magazine

items.title: Graduate Student Proves a Quantum Uncertainty Principle for Fractals
items.author: Shalma Wegsman
items.description: The math, which combines chaos, quantum theory, and infinitely complex fractal structures, has been called a “foundational result.” The post Graduate Student Proves a Quantum Uncertainty Principle for Fractals first appeared on Quanta Magazine
